newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Santander H1 net up as Latam surges.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Santander H1 net up as Latam surges.

text.p: Spain's largest bank, the Santander group, reported a jump of more than 30 percent in first-half earnings on Tuesday, as its Latin American shopping spree began to pay off.
Net attributable earnings climbed to 59.78 billion pesetas ($386 million) from 45.90 in the year-earlier period with Latin America contributing some 40 percent to that total.
"Latin America made an important contribution to group results from retail banking, investment banking and other financial services," Santander said in its report to shareholders.

"Excluding goodwill amortisation, and the financial costs associated with these investments, the combined contribution of retail banking and Santander Investment from this region came to 22.52 billion pesetas, well in line with the estimated income of $400 million for the full year," Santander said.
In the 1990s Santander has ploughed some $3.4 billion into the region, purchasing banks this year in Argentina, Brazil, Colombia and Venezuela.

Santander has said it is aiming for 50 percent of its earnings from abroad, as the bank diversifies in the face of narrowing domestic profit margins and revenue losses tied to the launch of Europe's single currency, set for 1999.
The first-half profit jump was well above analysts on average expectations for a rise of 20.8 percent in net attributable income and the bank said the group would continue to post sharp gains.
"It is reasonable to assume that the bank maintains these growth levels (for the full-year)," spokesman Federico Ysart told journalists at a briefing.
At home, basic lending and fee revenues performed well as at other Spanish banks.
Net interest income -- which shows revenues from loans after costs of deposits -- rose 27.5 percent in the first-half excluding dividend income.
"The overall results have been exceptional," Ysart said.
